Regime Ladder · research scaffold · deep dive

The horizon ladder and its intervals

The product: what is estimated and why it is measured at fixed horizons from a fresh unit rather than rolled forward from a daily rate, the two kinds of dependence between entries and the interval that respects both, shrinkage and what it costs, the increments that map the number onto an aged book, the persistence split and its identity, exact aggregation of base legs into any combination in vega units, the tenor curve, and the two gates the card has to pass. Every figure is from synthetic data with a known answer.

1The estimand built · validated on synthetic

EV(h | s) = mean over past entries made on days labelled s of [ cumulative net P&L from entry to day h ] held h days, no exit rule, hedged exactly as the backtester hedges, cash per unit of vega at inception

Everything on the card is this quantity or a statistic of the same sample: its quantiles, the probability it is positive, its expected shortfall, the count of independent episodes behind it. Three commitments follow from measuring it this way rather than estimating a daily rate per regime and adding days up.

  1. The exposure is right by construction. Every observation starts from a fresh unit and ages through the backtester's own repricing and hedging; nothing is rescaled by a Greek that was true on a different day.
  2. Transitions inside the window are already in the outcomes. A unit entered in carry that lived through a break to stressed on day 4 contributes exactly what it earned; no switch term is added and none can be double-counted. (That is also why the transition matrix is not an input to any number here.)
  3. The distribution is measured, not simulated. Tails and probability of profit are empirical quantiles of the same entries, never shrunk.
Read it as a market-maker. The base legs are the components a smile-vega-neutral book decomposes into; the ladder is the marginal expected earn of carrying one unit of a component for the next h days from today's state — a number to tilt composition with, not a trade signal. Short horizons are primary for a book that is re-cut continuously; the increments between horizons (Section 8) are how the number applies to inventory that is already days old.

2From trade-day rows to a rung built · validated on synthetic

The input is one row per trade per day: pair, archetype, tenor, entry date, date, age, net P&L, and where available the components (trade, delta hedge, vega hedge) and daily Greeks. cumulative sums each trade's rows to every horizon h ≤ tenor and to expiry; attach_entry_labels joins the point-in-time label on the entry date and drops (and counts) entries without one. A rung is the set of cumulative outcomes of all entries labelled s, at one h, in one (pair, archetype, tenor).

Horizons are capped at the component's tenor and the to-expiry rung is always added, so a 1W component has rungs 1 / 3 / 5 and a 1Y component gains 40 and 60. Entries without a label — the warm-up of the features, a gap in the surface — are dropped from every rung and reported as a count, never filled.

3Why the entries are not independent built · validated on synthetic

Entries are made every day and each lives h days, so consecutive entries share h − 1 of their days: the same daily shocks are in both outcomes. That is the overlap dependence and it has a known length, h. There is a second kind that outlasts it. Entries made inside the same regime episode share that episode's fate — when it ends and what it ends into — and for a quantity conditioned on the entry state, that is most of what varies between episodes. Two entries ten days apart in one long agitated episode are not independent at h = 5 even though their windows never touch.

n_eff ≈ n · min( 1 , entry spacing / h ) episodes = contiguous runs of the entry state in the label history

n_eff discounts the overlap; episodes count the fates. Both are on the card, because a cell with n_eff 40 from 4 episodes and a cell with n_eff 40 from 25 episodes are not equally trustworthy, and no single number says so.

4Intervals built · validated on synthetic

Four ways to put a 90% interval on a rung's mean, and what the synthetic truth says about each:

  1. Newey–West (HAC) with bandwidth h: a standard error that allows for autocorrelation up to lag h. Fast; exactly the overlap and nothing else.
  2. Circular block bootstrap with blocks of 2h: resample the ordered outcomes in blocks long enough to keep the overlap dependence inside a block.
  3. Episode-cluster bootstrap: resample whole regime episodes of entries with replacement — the unit the fate dependence lives in.
  4. The hybrid (default, ci: boot): the wider of 2 and 3, centred on the mean.

5Shrinkage built · validated on synthetic

A rung with little evidence is pulled toward the unconditional mean at the same horizon — the ALL row — with weight n_eff / (n_eff + κ). The tails are never shrunk: a quantile of a thin sample is reported as a quantile of a thin sample, with its episode count beside it.

mean_shrunk = w · mean_s + (1 − w) · mean_ALL w = n_eff / (n_eff + κ), κ = 20 by default

6The ladder built · validated on synthetic

7Increments: the aged unit built · validated on synthetic

The difference between consecutive rungs, divided by the days between them, is the expected earn per day of a unit that is already h days old over its next few days. A market-making book holds strikes of every age, so this row maps onto actual inventory where the ladder maps onto a fresh unit; and where a component stops earning per unit of risk, the roll point falls out of the chart.

increment(h₁→h₂) = ( EV(h₂) − EV(h₁) ) / (h₂ − h₁) Σ increments · days = EV(T) exactly

8Regime dependence: the persistence split built · validated on synthetic

Each rung's outcomes are split by whether the entry state was still in force on every day to h (persisted) or had left at least once (broke), with the break frequency q. It is a decomposition for explanation, never a forecast: it tells apart a component that is hurt by a break from one that is insurance against it, which the EV column cannot. The identity holds exactly in sample; the two parts are never multiplied together and never shown as a ratio.

(1 − q) · EV_persisted + q · EV_broke = EV

9Base legs, combinations and scaling built · validated on synthetic

The backtester runs five base legs per tenor — the ATM straddle, the 25d put and call, the 10d put and call — each hedged leg by leg. Because hedging is per leg and P&L is per leg per day, the daily P&L of any combination of legs entered on the same date is exactly the weighted sum of its legs', hedges included; a spread's ladder is the ladder of that summed series, with no new backtest run for any combination anyone cares to name. Rows are matched on (pair, tenor, entry date, age), so a combination row exists only where every leg has one.

Scaling. Each base leg's P&L is divided by its own vega at age 1 — the strategy's net vega excluding the vega-hedge leg, which is the leg's inception vega (from day 2 the daily vega hedge takes it to ~0, so inception is the only meaningful normaliser). Weights are then vega units: a zero-sum weight vector is smile-vega-neutral by construction (risk reversal = +1 call − 1 put; fly = +½ put + ½ call − 1 ATM) and a non-zero sum carries net vega, which is how a market-making book is decomposed. Packages the source also runs as packages are reconciled against the combination of their legs at WU-03 and are never themselves rescaled.

EV_combo(h | s) = Σ_i w_i · EV_leg i(h | s) exact for the mean (linearity); intervals, quantiles and ES need the combined rows

On the synthetic legs the combination reproduces the leg-level identity to machine precision (max |rr − (call − put)| = 0.0e+00). The linear EV is the cheap first pass over many candidates (screen); distributions are then computed for a shortlist.

10Tenors built · validated on synthetic

Any major tenor from 1W to 1Y is a separate component; the ladder is per (pair, leg or combination, tenor) and horizons are capped at tenor. At a fixed short horizon, EV across tenors is a tenor curve per component — which tenor's skew is best paid from here — and it makes the remaining-tenor diagnostic of the age-dependence question directly testable.

11What the card shows, and the gates it must pass built · validated on synthetic

Per component, per pair and tenor, for today's state: the rungs with EV, 90% interval, P(profit), ES 5%, n_eff and episodes; the persistence split at the longest rung; where it earns (the extreme increments); the state profile, tags, the shock score and the transition fan. Two pre-registered gates decide whether any of it is shown to a trader:

  • Gate 2 · separation. At h ≤ 10, the best and worst entry states differ by more than two standard errors in at least 75% of (component, h) cells. Synthetic: true labels pass (100% of cells), estimated labels pass (92%).
  • Gate 3 · go/no-go. Walk-forward by entry date (four test windows after a 40% training block, purged by h): the state-conditional prediction must beat the unconditional mean out of sample at every h ≤ 10 — positive MSE improvement, positive rank IC, calibration slope in [0.5, 1.5] — and (WU-11) beat a regularised model on the continuous features. Synthetic: true labels pass, estimated labels fail.

13On real data built · validated on synthetic WU-02, WU-03, WU-10, WU-11

  1. The vertical slice first (WU-02): one pair, the straddle, the ALL row at h = 5, reconciled against a direct pandas computation for one month of entries. Everything else is this, repeated.
  2. Legs before packages (WU-03): confirm per-day vega is available for the inception normaliser; reconcile the source's own RR and fly packages against combine of the legs — correlation ~1 and a stable ratio — before any combination is quoted.
  3. Intervals: hybrid, always. HAC is for speed in development. Read the episode column before the interval.
  4. κ by leave-one-fold-out MSE, and score the walk-forward at the κ the card shows (eval.kappa).
  5. Gate 3 against layer 1 as well as layer 0 (WU-11): the ridge model on the continuous features is the benchmark that decides whether discretising into states adds anything. If it does not, the states become presentation language over a continuous model — an acceptable outcome, stated as such.
  6. Failure modes. Entries dropped for missing labels concentrated in one period (the feature warm-up or a data gap — check before Gate 2); a persistence split with q ≈ 1 at h = 5 (the labeller is switching faster than the horizon — back to the switch budget); increments that change sign between adjacent buckets in every state (an attribution artefact at drifted strikes, the age-dependence question).
